summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a complex medical history including kidney transplantation, chronic kidney disease stage 4, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and recent pericarditis was admitted for persistent epigastric pain and poor appetite following his prior discharge. CT imaging revealed findings consistent with diverticulitis, without perforation or abscess. He was treated with intravenous Unasyn followed by oral Augmentin, with clinical improvement. Due to a history of recurrent C. difficile, prophylactic oral vancomycin was initiated. His abdominal pain resolved, he tolerated oral intake, and inflammatory markers improved. Chronic conditions, including pericarditis, heart failure, and transplant management, were maintained on stable regimens. He was discharged home with a plan for completion of antibiotics, close primary follow-up, and outpatient colonoscopy to evaluate for underlying colonic pathology.
problems: Diverticulitis of large intestine without perforation or abscess without bleeding
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
